Stop Blaming Frameworks Most Slow JavaScript Comes From These Simple Mistakes

4 min read
Just now

--

Press enter or click to view image in full size

Every JavaScript developer has experienced this.
You build a feature.
It works perfectly.
Then someone opens it on an older laptop or a mid-range phone…
Suddenly the UI freezes, animations stutter, and users start closing the page before it even finishes loading.
At first, I blamed React.
Then I blamed Chrome.
Then I blamed my computer.
Eventually I realized something surprising:
Most performance problems weren’t caused by JavaScript itself. They were caused by the way I was writing JavaScript.
After profiling dozens of projects, I discovered a handful of habits that consistently made my applications noticeably faster.
Here are the ones that made the biggest difference.
1. Cache DOM Elements Instead of Querying Them Repeatedly
One of the easiest mistakes is repeatedly searching the DOM.
